facts.heading: Tomas is nervous about therapy
facts.content: Tomas is nervous about attending therapy.
facts.evidence: I am quite nervous, if I am to be honest.

facts.heading: Wife prompted therapy attendance
facts.content: Tomas's wife suggested he seek therapy because the current situation could not continue.
facts.evidence: My wife. She says it can't go on like this.

facts.heading: Compulsive checking behavior
facts.content: Tomas checks if he locked the door and turned off the stove thirty times per night.
facts.evidence: Thirty times a night I check if I locked the door and turned off the stove,

facts.heading: Time taken to leave apartment
facts.content: It takes Tomas one hour to leave his apartment.
facts.evidence: it takes me an hour to leave the apartment.

facts.heading: Checking routine details
facts.content: Tomas's routine involves locking the door, going to the elevator, returning to pull the handle, checking the stove knobs separately, and checking the door again.
facts.evidence: I lock the door, I go to the elevator, I come back and pull the handle. Then I check the stove, every knob separately. Then the door again.

facts.heading: Relief followed by intrusive thought
facts.content: After checking, Tomas feels relieved temporarily, but then an image comes to mind that he didn't check properly, leading him to check again.
facts.evidence: I feel relieved for a while. And then an image comes into my head that I didn't do it properly, and I have to do it again.

facts.heading: Intrusive fire image
facts.content: Tomas sees a clear image of the apartment on fire after checking.
facts.evidence: The apartment on fire. I see it clearly, like a film.

facts.heading: Frequency of intrusive images
facts.content: The intrusive images happen every day, worst in the evening and in the morning.
facts.evidence: Every day. It's the worst in the evening when we go out or go to sleep. In the morning too.

facts.heading: Fire incident started two years ago
facts.content: The issue started two years ago after the neighbors' house caught fire and they had to evacuate.
facts.evidence: It started two years ago when the neighbors' house caught fire and we had to evacuate.

facts.heading: Experience of neighbor's fire
facts.content: Tomas was woken by the alarm during the neighbor's fire, seeing smoke in the hallway and people screaming.
facts.evidence: The alarm woke me up. There was smoke in the hallway and people were screaming.

facts.heading: Feeling of personal blame
facts.content: Since the fire, Tomas feels he can cause it and that if he doesn't control something, it will happen and he will be to blame.
facts.evidence: Since then I have the feeling that I can cause it. That if I don't control something, it will happen and I will be to blame.

facts.heading: Anxiety response to not checking
facts.content: When Tomas resists checking, anxiety grows until he feels like he is going crazy, making him prefer to check.
facts.evidence: And then anxiety grows in me, until I feel like I'm going crazy. I'd rather do it.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms of anxiety
facts.content: Tomas experiences heart symptoms, sweating, shaking hands, and stomach sickness when anxious.
facts.evidence: Heart, sweat. My hands shake and I feel sick in my stomach.

facts.heading: Wife knows about the issue
facts.content: Tomas's wife, Barbora, knows about his issue.
facts.evidence: Barbora. My wife.

facts.heading: Wife's perception of the issue
facts.content: Barbora initially viewed the behavior as a habit, but now she sees it is more serious.
facts.evidence: At first she took it as a habit, now she sees that it's more.

facts.heading: Late arrival at cinema
facts.content: Tomas arrived at the cinema forty minutes late yesterday.
facts.evidence: Yesterday we arrived at the cinema forty minutes later.

facts.heading: Wife's reaction to delay
facts.content: Barbora waited outside for Tomas to return and check the stove for the third time, looking at him without speaking.
facts.evidence: She waited outside for me to return and check the stove for the third time. She didn't say anything, she just looked at me.

facts.heading: Tomas's work as electrician
facts.content: Tomas works as an electrician in Olomouc. He does wiring in apartments and sometimes in houses.
facts.evidence: I work as an electrician in Olomouc. I do wiring in apartments and sometimes in houses.

facts.heading: Fear of making wiring mistake
facts.content: Tomas is afraid he will make a mistake connecting a wire incorrectly and something will burn.
facts.evidence: I'm afraid that because of my head I will make a mistake once. That I will connect a wire incorrectly and something will burn.

facts.heading: Checking behavior after jobs
facts.content: Tomas checks after every job he does. Sometimes he goes back the next day just to look.
facts.evidence: after every job I go back and check. Sometimes I go back the next day, just to look.

facts.heading: Colleagues view Tomas as pedant
facts.content: Tomas's colleagues think he is a pedant.
facts.evidence: They think I'm a pedant.

facts.heading: Boss notes Tomas's carefulness
facts.content: Tomas's boss says he is the most careful in the company.
facts.evidence: The boss tells me I'm the most careful in the company

facts.heading: Checking costs work time
facts.content: The checking behavior adds an hour of work to Tomas every day in the last few months.
facts.evidence: In the last few months, it adds an hour of work to me every day.

facts.heading: Tomas handed over jobs
facts.content: Tomas has handed over a few jobs to a colleague because he didn't have time.
facts.evidence: I have already handed over a few jobs to a colleague because I didn't have time.

facts.heading: Fear of losing job now
facts.content: Tomas is afraid he will lose his job, especially now.
facts.evidence: I'm afraid I'll lose my job. Especially now.

facts.heading: Barbora is four months pregnant
facts.content: Barbora is four months pregnant.
facts.evidence: Barbora is four months pregnant.

facts.heading: Tomas felt happy about pregnancy
facts.content: Tomas was happy about the pregnancy.
facts.evidence: I was happy. Really.

facts.heading: Waited for pregnancy three years
facts.content: Tomas and Barbora waited for the pregnancy for three years.
facts.evidence: We waited for it for three years.

facts.heading: Intrusive thoughts of harming
facts.content: Tomas has thoughts that he will harm Barbora and the baby.
facts.evidence: That I will harm her and the baby.

facts.heading: Thoughts occur during daily tasks
facts.content: Tomas fears the thought of harming them might happen while cutting bread or standing by the stairs.
facts.evidence: maybe when I'm cutting bread or standing by the stairs.

facts.heading: Tomas has never told anyone
facts.content: Tomas has never told anyone about the intrusive thoughts, not even Barbora.
facts.evidence: I've never told anyone about it, not even Barbora.

facts.heading: Leaving room or checking helps
facts.content: When the thought appears, Tomas either leaves the room or goes back to check something to make it stop.
facts.evidence: I leave the room. Or I go back and check something to make it stop.

facts.heading: Checking helps calm thoughts
facts.content: Tomas believes checking helps calm the intrusive thoughts.
facts.evidence: Actually, yes. It never occurred to me that they were related.

facts.heading: Sleep problems with checking stove
facts.content: Tomas sleeps terribly and wakes up twice at night to check the stove.
facts.evidence: I wake up twice at night and check the stove, even if there is nothing on it.

facts.heading: Walks help Tomas
facts.content: Going for walks with Barbora helps Tomas.
facts.evidence: Going for walks with Barbora helps me.

facts.heading: Home repairs keep Tomas busy
facts.content: Fixing something at home keeps Tomas busy.
facts.evidence: Or when I fix something at home, it keeps me busy.

facts.heading: Walks twice weekly
facts.content: Tomas goes for walks twice a week.
facts.evidence: Walks twice a week

facts.heading: Goals for future
facts.content: Tomas wants to leave the apartment in five minutes. He also wants to look forward to a child without certain thoughts.
facts.evidence: To leave the apartment in five minutes. And to look forward to a child without those thoughts.

facts.heading: Fear of exposure therapy
facts.content: Tomas was afraid of therapy where a person is gradually exposed to what they are afraid of.
facts.evidence: I was afraid of that.

facts.heading: Fear of forced exposure
facts.content: Tomas feared someone would force him to leave the door open and go.
facts.evidence: I thought someone would force me to leave the door open and go.

facts.heading: Difficulty with small steps
facts.content: Tomas finds even checking the door once to be a big step for him.
facts.evidence: But even that is big for me.

facts.heading: Feelings toward Barbora
facts.content: Tomas loves Barbora and feels he needs treatment so he doesn't lose her.
facts.evidence: That I love her. And that I need to get treated so I don't lose her.

facts.heading: Fear of Barbora's reaction
facts.content: Tomas is afraid that Barbora would not want to be with him.
facts.evidence: Right now I'm afraid she wouldn't want to be with me.

facts.heading: Barbora's expected reaction
facts.content: Tomas believes Barbora would probably hug him.
facts.evidence: She would probably hug me.

facts.heading: Agreement to try door check
facts.content: Tomas agreed to try checking the door once when he leaves the apartment.
facts.evidence: Once. I'll try it.

facts.heading: Plan to rate door check
facts.content: Tomas plans to write down a number from one to ten regarding the door check.
facts.evidence: I'll write down a number from one to ten.
